universal_lens: Self-supervised learning frameworks unify detection and tracking through latent representation alignment across temporal frames. A unified framework for soccer player detection and tracking using FPN-FasterRCNN and appearance embedding with triplet loss.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference models player states via probabilistic tracking, integrating visual features with tactical priors for game interpretation. Bayesian inference models player states and transitions using probabilistic tracking with conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions map player motion and positional shifts using dynamic constraint graphs derived from tracked trajectories. Situational reasoning engine maps player positions and actions through state-transition graphs informed by real-time visual data and motion dynamics.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter window 4 focuses on refining field detection in unlabeled soccer videos using a multi-step pipeline. The process begins with extracting wide-view frames from the SoccerNet dataset, which provides a rich source of unlabeled data for training. The core innovation lies in applying a green filter to isolate potential field pixels, followed by morphological operations to refine the mask. A key challenge arises from the presence of coaches in the green bottom portion of the field, which must be excluded to avoid false positives. To address this, a bottom-line detection mechanism using the Hough transform is employed. This method leverages the pix2pix model to generate an initial binary approximation of field lines, which are then processed through Hough line detection to extract precise geometric features. The resulting field mask serves as a foundational spatial reference for subsequent player detection and tracking tasks. The robustness of this approach hinges on accurate color thresholding and spatial exclusion protocols, ensuring that the inferred field geometry aligns with real-world expectations. The integration of these primitives into the broader GSI and GSE frameworks enables scalable, context-aware analysis of broadcast soccer content.
